objective: Formalize all 137 exact sampler entries in the frozen queue using the verification and polishing protocol, independent review, and multiple passes.

baseline.historical_review_status: Historical receipts retain their original dependency context. A successful build against the new pin is compatibility evidence, not renewed independent review.

All p,q : unitInterval with p>0 or q>0, and arbitrary abstract callbacks for both input biases. Exactly the nonterminating zero-zero pair is excluded; law p^q.

Output RealCoin.law target, Bool encoding.

Every positive rational shape A/B and success probability s/t with naturals A, B, s > 0 and s <= t, including s = t (point mass at zero) and shapes below one; every other integer input makes the source fail, so the domain is complete. Positive rational alpha and beta, including subunit and unreduced shapes; zero-based failures before the first marked draw.
Any positive rational shape, including subunit and unreduced shapes; positive integer output, obtained by adding one to the beta-geometric failure count.

Any indexed fresh continuation-coin family, queried only at positive source indices, whose survival product from the first index tends to zero. No geometric rate, finite mean, or uniform-integer primitive assumption is required. The output is the positive first stopping index.

All positive rational alpha and nonnegative rational nu with alpha < nu+1, represented by unreduced natural numerator/positive denominator pairs. Includes nu=0 and alpha>1 where admissible. Output is positive; no finite-mean assumption.
Every a,b : Nat with b>0 and every p : unitInterval; arbitrary input callback, includes exponent0 and both input endpoints.

Every rational exponent a/b > 1 with naturals 0 < b < a; integer inputs with b <= 0 or a <= b make the source fail, so the domain is complete. The law on the naturals has no mass at 0 and mass (n+1)^(-a/b) / sum_m (m+1)^(-a/b) at n+1; the output is Val.int n. Arbitrary ENNReal credit, including infinity, is supported. No externally assumed sampler callbacks are needed.

Every positive finite bound n and nonnegative rational exponent a/b, with natural a and positive natural b. The target law is on Fin n and the actual output integer is k+1. Arbitrary ENNReal credit, including infinity, is supported. No externally assumed sampler callbacks are needed.

Any positive finite support size and monotone real-valued finite CDF reaching one, including irrational masses and zero-mass plateaus. Valid dyadic enclosure callbacks are required only at in-range indices.
Any finite list of positive-total nonnegative integer rows and any valid row index; rectangular matrices and zero weights are permitted.

Any initial owned cache, index and arbitrarily tight valid dyadic threshold enclosures. The returned comparison keeps the same latent uniform, refined prefix and arbitrary joint output/latent credits.

Arbitrarily tight dyadic probability enclosures, not necessarily nested and with no known convergence rate; both probability endpoints allowed. Bounds callbacks return the actual positive-level lower/upper numerators.
Any probability proposal on a measurable output type, measurable positive-mass acceptance set (including mass one), a proposal IsDistSpec and a correct deterministic membership-test specification.

Every finite natural weight list with positive total and every owned alias table whose category mass equals length times the corresponding weight; zero-weight categories are allowed and both arrays are retained.

Every finite natural-weight list with positive total, encoded as integer list values: zero-weight rows, a certain row (repaired all-ones endpoint, e.g. [2,0] and [0,0,5]), the length-one shortcut, exact totals 2^k-2^l without padding and padded totals with an appended rejection label. The full canonical weighted-choice law on original integer position labels supports arbitrary ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity.

Every valid cyclic probability table given as the source tuple (matrix,(k,(l,rejected))): arbitrary natural rows rows : Fin n -> N (bits above 2^k ignored, as the scan reads only the low k bits), any l<k, any integer rejection label (outside [0,n) means no rejection), cyclic row numerators summing to 2^k-2^l (total mass one), and positive accepted mass (rejected row mass below one, any rejection probability below one). The law is the canonical weighted-choice law on row labels of the accepted numerators, for arbitrary ENNReal continuation credit including infinity.

Every positive-total natural-weight list that is monotone (nondecreasing or nonincreasing), including zero rows, constant lists, all-zero envelope groups and the length-one shortcut. Unsorted lists fail the source's adjacent-pair check, so this is the complete domain. FLDR's IsDistSpec is used at every group draw. The full canonical weighted-choice law on original integer position labels supports arbitrary ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity.

Every finite natural-weight list with positive total and either density 2^19*length<=sum, or all weights strictly below2^32. Dense lists may contain arbitrarily large weights. Sparse packed lists satisfy precisely the source32-bit field guard. The full canonical weighted-choice law on original integer position labels supports arbitrary ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity.

All positive-total natural weights, count≤population length, and count*weight≤total at each position. Includes zero weights, full samples and capacity equality. A separate zero-count theorem covers every natural-weight list, including empty/all-zero populations, without uniform-integer assumptions. The target is the exact ordered full joint splitting law, with fixed size, no duplicates and prescribed inclusion probabilities.

Any finite nonnegative integer weight list of positive total, natural count at most the population size, and count*weight<=total for each item. A supplementary zero-count spec covers every natural weight list, including empty/all-zero populations, without uniform-integer assumptions.

Every finite natural-weight list with positive total, including zero rows, certain rows and singletons; negative or zero-total inputs make the source fail. The source pads the total to the next power of two with one implicit rejection row that restarts the walk and is never returned. The full canonical weighted-choice law on original integer position labels supports arbitrary ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity.

Every finite natural-weight vector of positive total, including zero weights, non-dyadic probabilities and certain rows. The output is the original-position integer label with the canonical categorical law. Arbitrary ENNReal output credit, including infinity, is supported; no finite runtime or continuation-moment premise is required.

Every finite natural-weight list with positive total, including zero weights, certain rows, dyadic and non-dyadic probabilities. The full canonical weighted-choice law uses original position labels. All measurable ENNReal output credit, including infinity, is allowed.

Every positive bound n and nonnegative count, including count 0; recycledSamples_zero_distSpec additionally covers count 0 for every integer bound. Negative counts fail at the source guard, and a positive count with n <= 0 fails in recycledUniform, so the domain is complete. The law is count IID uniform draws on [0,n), decoded as a list in sampling order. Arbitrary ENNReal credit, including infinity, is supported. The internal fresh pool is allocated and dropped.

Every positive bound n with an owned pool holding the reset state (0,1); n <= 0 makes the source fail. The output is uniform on [0,n) as Val.int r and the owned pool is returned holding (0,1). The reset state is the only reachable pool state in the source: newRecycler allocates (0,1), and from (0,1) every acceptance has quotient one, so the store writes (0,1). Arbitrary ENNReal credit, including infinity, is supported. The stronger joint theorem twp_recycledUniform covers every valid stored rank value < width.

All p : unitInterval, including p=0 via continuous extension atan(p)/p=1; arbitrary input callback IsDistSpec without closedness assumption.

The actual accepted oracle and its refined posterior/ownership are retained; arbitrary measurable joint ENNReal credits are supported.

Construction of one ideal unit-uniform deferred real; every natural observation precision, including zero and repeated/decreasing reads, through aliases of the same returned closure. The actual heap root and arbitrary measurable joint posterior ENNReal credit are preserved.

An owned deferred real oracle with measurable errors, AE nonnegative values, and either global AE avoidance of the integer grid or global AE first-observation error zero. The conditional bias is exp(-value) almost everywhere. The same source ownership and admissibility invariant are retained with arbitrary measurable joint output/world ENNReal credit, including infinity.

All strictly positive integer numerator and denominator, representing every positive rational rate, including unreduced fractions. Each returns a canonical Exp(rate) deferred real with one retained whole/fraction joint world. Every finite observation precision, repeated alias, arbitrary measurable whole-world ENNReal credit and infinity is supported.

Every positive finite real rate, supplied through a unary callback whose ordinary compositional contract gives an exact exp(-rate/d) coin at each positive natural divisor d. The sampler owns one whole/fraction joint world, returns a shared deferred exponential oracle with the canonical Exp(rate) law, and supports every finite precision and arbitrary measurable joint ENNReal credit, including infinity.

Every pair of integers with 0<y<x, representing rate log(x/y). Each returns a canonical Exp(rate) deferred real with one retained whole/fraction joint world. Every finite observation precision, repeated alias, arbitrary measurable whole-world ENNReal credit and infinity is supported.

Every supplied ordinary coin of unknown positive bias p in (0,1], including p=1. The implementation is over real ProbLang with UniformInt and UniformReal, as required by its actual exponential factory; rational and logarithmic wrappers need UniformInt only. Each returns a canonical Exp(rate) deferred real with one retained whole/fraction joint world. Every finite observation precision, repeated alias, arbitrary measurable whole-world ENNReal credit and infinity is supported.

Every dimension n>=1; n<=0 fails in the actual source guard. Target law: uniform on the open standard simplex, i.e. m! times Lebesgue measure on {y>0, sum y<1} in R^m embedded by appending 1-sum y (n=m+1), proved for the spec's own world/output/initial (output_law_uniform). The result is the actual list of n jointly owned deferred coordinate oracles over one unit-rate exponential world (n=1: constant 1/1, world unobserved; n>=2: actual exponentials normalized by one shared sum), with arbitrary joint ENNReal credits including infinity, all natural read precisions and repeated aliases. Only UniformInt randomness is needed.

Every probability measure on an arbitrary measurable latent world, with any measurable Bool digit stream and a verified callback supplying its conditional next-bit law at each positive-mass reachable prefix. Digits may be dependent or atomic. The owned deferred real is the full binary-stream value, including the all-ones value one. All finite precisions, repeated aliases, arbitrary measurable whole-world ENNReal credit and infinity are supported.

Target law U/(1-U) for one unit uniform U, identified as the shifted Pareto(1,1) with CDF t/(1+t); numerator and complement read one cache. The unit argument only (the source has no guard). The returned closure is the actual lazy oracle; every finite precision and repeated alias retains its ownership and arbitrary measurable joint latent-world ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity. Only UniformInt randomness is needed.

Target law U^(a/b) for one unit uniform U. Every integer numerator a and natural denominator b>0 (passed as #int b); b<=0 fails in powerRational's guard. All branches: a=0 constant 1/1, a>0 with b=1 repeated squaring, a>0 with b>=2 bisection root, a<0 reciprocal of either. Root.Admissible and the reciprocal's nonzero denominator are proved under every posterior from u>0 a.s. Every finite precision and repeated alias retains the one uniform's ownership and arbitrary measurable joint latent-world ENNReal credit, including infinity. Only UniformInt randomness is needed.

Target law U/V for independent unit uniforms U, V (Occil's Lazy[U/V]), as the pushforward of the product uniform by division; both caches live in one product world. The unit argument only (the source has no guard). The returned closure is the actual lazy oracle; every finite precision and repeated alias retains its ownership and arbitrary measurable joint latent-world ENNReal continuation credit, including infinity. Only UniformInt randomness is needed.

Target law U^(-a/b) for one unit uniform U, via the actual reciprocal of newPowerUniform's oracle. Every integer numerator a and natural denominator b>0 (passed as #int b); b<=0 fails in powerRational's guard. All branches: a=0 constant 1/1, a>0 with b=1 repeated squaring, a>0 with b>=2 bisection root, a<0 reciprocal of either. Root.Admissible and the reciprocal's nonzero denominator are proved under every posterior from u>0 a.s. Every finite precision and repeated alias retains the one uniform's ownership and arbitrary measurable joint latent-world ENNReal credit, including infinity. Only UniformInt randomness is needed.

The parameter-free reciprocal of a single unit-uniform deferred real, with canonical Pareto(scale=1,shape=1) law. Every finite observation precision and repeated alias is supported. The one underlying uniform cache and arbitrary measurable whole-world ENNReal credit, including infinity, are retained.

Every natural number of summands, including zero. The actual returned interval oracle owns one nested product world of uniform sources, preserves arbitrary measurable joint ENNReal credits and supports every natural precision and repeated aliases. Its observable law is the canonical Irwin–Hall convolution, with a point mass at zero for no summands.

Every nonnegative natural numerator and positive natural denominator, with any input Bernoulli probability in the closed unit interval and a correctly specified ordinary input-coin callback. Includes p=0, p=1, exponent zero with0^0=1, integral and fractional exponents, and arbitrary ENNReal continuation credits.
